services.title: Find your study space
services.subtitle: A little focus. A lot of possibility.
services.description: Get your group together or find a place to focus. Reserve study rooms at Morisset, the Brian Dickson Law Library, Learning Crossroads (5th floor), and the Health Sciences Library through the official booking system.
services.note: Room availability and booking conditions are shown in the official system. Saving here does not reserve a room.
steps: Choose a library location with your group.
Open the official room booking system.
Review availability, sign in there, and confirm your reservation.

services.title: Make sense of your research
services.subtitle: Start with a question, leave with a direction.
services.description: Find a research guide for your subject and contact the librarian or specialist listed on that guide. Get help with research, databases, and resources for an assignment.
services.note: Prepare your assignment question before contacting a librarian. Appointment arrangements are handled by the Library.
steps: Write down your research question and assignment requirements.
Find your subject in the research guides.
Contact the librarian or specialist listed in your guide.

services.title: Your voice. Studio quality.
services.subtitle: That podcast idea? Make it real.
services.description: Two podcast studios with professional microphones, mixers and soundproofing. One has four microphones and phone Bluetooth connectivity; the other has two microphones. Staff can help with scripting, recording and editing.
services.note: Request a booking using the contact link on the official page. This app cannot confirm a studio or time slot.
steps: Outline your recording and how many speakers you need.
Open the official Podcasting page and choose Send your request.
Arrange your time and support needs with the Digital Skills Hub team.

services.title: Get the tools you need
services.subtitle: Big ideas deserve the right equipment.
services.description: Explore multimedia equipment for schoolwork and research through the official equipment catalogue. Library computers provide access to software, and uOLabsPlus offers selected applications remotely to eligible users.
services.note: Equipment availability, eligibility and loan conditions must be checked with the Library. No stock or laptop availability is claimed here.
steps: List the equipment or software your project needs.
Check the multimedia equipment catalogue or uOLabsPlus links.
Confirm access, loan terms and pickup details with the Library.

services.title: Cite with confidence
services.subtitle: Give your sources the credit they deserve.
services.description: Learn about citation styles, citation management software, choosing sources and avoiding plagiarism. The Library provides tutorials and resources designed for undergraduate students and novice researchers.
services.note: Follow the citation style requested by your instructor. These links teach citation practices; this app does not generate or verify citations.
steps: Check which citation style your instructor requires.
Read the Library citation-style guide.
Explore a citation manager and review your references.

services.title: Learn something that clicks
services.subtitle: Small sessions. Skills that stay with you.
services.location: Online & in person · Check each session
services.description: Discover workshops, training and tours that build library, research and digital skills. Use the official listing for current topics, dates, registration details and delivery format.
services.note: The page also contains past sessions. Check the year and registration status before making plans; no upcoming session is assumed here.
steps: Choose a skill you want to build.
Find a session and check its date, year and delivery format.
Register through the official listing if registration is open.

services.title: Meet your creative side
services.subtitle: A space to try something completely new.
services.description: Discover virtual reality, gaming, data visualization and digital content creation. The Digital Skills Hub supports students, faculty and staff, with priority for research and educational projects.
services.note: Contact the team for the current process, suitable equipment and support for your project.
steps: Choose your project: video, VR or data visualization.
Explore the relevant Digital Skills Hub service.
Contact the team about access and project support.

services.title: Study your way
services.subtitle: Support that makes room for you.
services.description: Find accessible study rooms, adjustable workstations, assistive software and accessible library materials. The official page explains how to request access to book an assistive workstation.
services.note: Share any accommodation needs directly with the Library. GeeGuide never asks for diagnoses or disability information.
steps: Review the accessible spaces and software offered.
Contact the Library directly about the support you need.
Follow the official access and booking instructions.

services.title: Your student card opens doors
services.subtitle: Books, resources, and your next discovery.
services.description: Your student card serves as your library card. Your uoAccess credentials provide access to electronic resources and your Omni account. Explore how to borrow and access resources as a student.
services.note: Use your institutional credentials only on official university services. No student number or password is collected here.
steps: Bring your student card when visiting the Library.
Explore Omni and the student library guide.
Check borrowing conditions for the material you need.

services.title: A real person, ready to help
services.subtitle: You do not have to figure it out alone.
services.description: Reach Library staff through the official contact page, check chat and text schedules, or find a subject librarian. The Library lists 613-562-5213 for help during opening hours.
services.note: Check official contact schedules and library hours. Opening hours and response times are not live in this prototype.
steps: Write down what you need help with.
Choose chat, phone, in-person or librarian support on the official page.
Check service hours before reaching out.
